evidence: Isid. Sent. 2.13.7: quasi sī quis lavet laterem crūdum, quem quantō magis ēlāverit, tantō amplius lutum facit
terms.comment: “You are washing an unbaked brick”: the fuller form of Terence’s proverb, in Isidore, of a man who repents and sins again; the more he washes the brick, the more mud he makes.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Isidore, Sententiae 2.13.7, checked against the Latin Library text.
